fr.B: Ma maison n’est-elle pas ainsi auprès de Dieu ? \q Car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a conclu avec moi une alliance éternelle, réglée en tout point et assurée. \q Tout mon salut et tout mon désir, ne les fera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pas grandir ?
fr.R: N’est-ce pas ainsi que Dieu traite ma famille ? \q Il a fait avec moi une alliance qui durera toujours ; elle est bien réglée et sûre en tout. \q Oui, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fera grandir et fleurir mon salut et tout ce que je désire !

sw.L: Kwa maana je, nyumba yangu si hivyo kwa Mungu? \q Kwa maana amefanya nami agano la milele, lililopangwa katika [mambo] yote na kulindwa; \q kwa maana wokovu wangu wote na [haja] yangu yote, je, hataichipusha?
sw.B: Je, nyumba yangu si hivyo mbele za Mungu? \q Kwa maana amefanya nami agano la milele, lililopangwa vizuri kila upande na kuwekwa salama. \q Wokovu wangu wote na kila ninalotamani, je, hatayakuza?
sw.R: Je, hivi sivyo Mungu anavyoitendea jamaa yangu? \q Amefanya nami agano litakalodumu milele; limepangwa vizuri na liko salama kwa kila njia. \q Hakika atafanya wokovu wangu na yote ninayoyatamani yakue na kustawi!

vi.L: Vì nhà tôi chẳng phải như vậy với Đức Chúa Trời sao? \q Vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã lập với tôi một giao ước đời đời, được sắp đặt trong mọi [điều] và được giữ vững; \q vì mọi sự cứu rỗi của tôi và mọi [điều tôi] ao ước, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chẳng làm cho [nó] nảy nở sao?
vi.B: Nhà tôi chẳng phải như thế trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời sao? \q Vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã lập với tôi một giao ước đời đời, được sắp đặt chu đáo mọi mặt và được giữ vững. \q Mọi sự cứu rỗi và mọi ước nguyện của tôi, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chẳng làm cho lớn lên sao?
vi.R: Chẳng phải Đức Chúa Trời đối xử với gia đình tôi như thế sao? \q Ngài đã lập với tôi một giao ước còn mãi mãi; giao ước ấy được sắp đặt chu đáo và vững chắc mọi mặt. \q Chắc chắn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ làm cho sự cứu rỗi của tôi và mọi điều tôi mong ước lớn lên và thịnh vượng!

decisions.choice: is not my house like this with God? a question expecting the answer yes
alternatives: Truly my house is not so with God
decisions.reason: The words can be read as a statement, "my house is not so with God", a humble admission that David's family has not lived up to the picture of the righteous ruler. They are taken here as a question that expects "yes", because the next line gives the reason with "for": God has made an everlasting covenant with David. The last line of the verse is a question of the same kind.

decisions.choice: an everlasting covenant: God's promise of a lasting dynasty in 2 Samuel 7
decisions.reason: Through Nathan God promised David that his house, his kingdom and his throne would be established forever (7:12-16). David's last words rest on that promise. Psalm 89:4-5, 29-30 also calls it a covenant.

decisions.choice: ordered and secured: set out in full and kept safe
decisions.reason: "Ordered" is used of things arranged in order, such as a battle line or a legal case; "secured" means guarded or kept. The covenant is complete in every part and God watches over it.

decisions.choice: all my salvation and all my desire, he will make grow: God will bring David's rescue and hopes to full growth
decisions.reason: "Salvation" here is God's rescue and help for David and his house. The verb means to make a plant sprout. It links with the growing grass of verse 4 and with the later hope of a "branch" from David (Jeremiah 23:5; Zechariah 3:8, using the noun from the same root).

decisions.choice: Surely he will make ... grow and flourish (statement)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the closing question, which expects the answer yes, into a strong statement. It says "family" for "house" in the first line.

source.text: וּבְלִיַּ֕עַל כְּק֥וֹץ מֻנָ֖ד כֻּלָּ֑הַם כִּֽי־לֹ֥א בְיָ֖ד יִקָּֽחוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And worthlessness, like thorn chased away [are] all of them, for not with hand will they be taken.

en.L: But [the] worthless [are] like thorns thrown away, all of them, \q for they are not taken with [the] hand.
en.B: But the worthless are all like thorns that are tossed aside, \q for no one picks them up by hand.
en.R: But wicked people are all like thorns that are thrown away. \q No one can pick them up with bare hands.

es.L: Pero los perversos [son] como espinos arrojados, todos ellos, \q porque no se toman con la mano.
es.B: Pero los perversos son todos como espinos que se echan a un lado, \q porque nadie los recoge con la mano.
es.R: Pero los malvados son todos como espinos que se tiran. \q Nadie puede recogerlos con las manos desnudas.

fr.L: Mais les vauriens, [ils sont] comme des épines qu’on rejette, tous, \q car on ne les prend pas avec la main.
fr.B: Mais les vauriens sont tous comme des épines qu’on jette de côté, \q car personne ne les ramasse à la main.
fr.R: Mais les méchants sont tous comme des épines qu’on jette. \q Personne ne peut les ramasser à mains nues.

sw.L: Lakini wasiofaa kitu [ni] kama miiba iliyotupwa mbali, wote, \q kwa maana hawashikwi kwa mkono.
sw.B: Lakini wasiofaa kitu wote ni kama miiba inayotupwa kando, \q kwa maana hakuna anayeiokota kwa mkono.
sw.R: Lakini watu waovu wote ni kama miiba inayotupwa. \q Hakuna mtu anayeweza kuiokota kwa mikono mitupu.

vi.L: Nhưng kẻ vô lại [thì] như gai bị ném bỏ, tất cả bọn chúng, \q vì người ta không lấy tay mà nhặt chúng.
vi.B: Nhưng những kẻ vô lại đều như gai góc bị vứt bỏ, \q vì không ai lấy tay nhặt chúng lên.
vi.R: Nhưng những kẻ gian ác đều như gai góc bị vứt bỏ. \q Không ai dám nhặt chúng lên bằng tay không.

decisions.choice: worthless: people who are good for nothing and do harm, the opposite of the righteous ruler
decisions.reason: The word, often "sons of worthlessness", is used of wicked and lawless people (1 Samuel 2:12; 25:17; 2 Samuel 16:7; 20:1). Here it stands against the righteous ruler of verses 3-4.

decisions.choice: thorns thrown away, not picked up by hand: something useless and hurtful that is cleared off and destroyed
decisions.reason: Thorny brush was cleared from fields with tools and burned (verse 7). Nobody gathers it with bare hands. The wicked bring only harm, and their end is to be cleared away.

decisions.choice: wicked people
decisions.reason: Readable says "wicked people", since "worthless" alone could sound like a comment on someone's value rather than on their evil ways.

source.text: וְאִישׁ֙ יִגַּ֣ע בָּהֶ֔ם יִמָּלֵ֥א בַרְזֶ֖ל וְעֵ֣ץ חֲנִ֑ית וּבָאֵ֕שׁ שָׂר֥וֹף יִשָּׂרְפ֖וּ בַּשָּֽׁבֶת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And a man [who] touches them is filled [with] iron and wood of a spear, and in fire burning they will be burned in the dwelling.

en.L: And {{gender:anyone|a man}} [who] touches them \q arms himself [with] iron and [the] shaft of a spear, \q and with fire they will be completely burned on the spot.
en.B: Whoever touches them \q must be armed with iron or the shaft of a spear, \q and they are burned up completely with fire where they lie.
en.R: Anyone who touches them \q needs an iron tool or the wooden handle of a spear. \q They are burned up in a fire right where they are.

es.L: Y el que los toca \q se arma [de] hierro y [del] asta de una lanza, \q y con fuego serán quemados del todo en el lugar.
es.B: Quien los toque \q tiene que ir armado de hierro o del asta de una lanza, \q y son quemados por completo con fuego allí donde están.
es.R: El que los toque \q necesita una herramienta de hierro o el mango de madera de una lanza. \q Los queman en el fuego allí mismo donde están.

fr.L: Et {{gender:quiconque|l’homme qui}} les touche \q s’arme de fer et du bois d’une lance, \q et par le feu ils seront entièrement brûlés sur place.
fr.B: Celui qui les touche \q doit s’armer de fer ou du bois d’une lance, \q et on les brûle entièrement au feu là où ils sont.
fr.R: Celui qui veut les toucher \q a besoin d’un outil en fer ou du manche en bois d’une lance. \q On les brûle dans un feu, là où ils sont.

sw.L: Na mtu anayeigusa \q hujivika chuma na mpini wa mkuki, \q nayo huteketezwa kabisa kwa moto papo hapo.
sw.B: Yeyote anayeigusa \q lazima awe na chuma au mpini wa mkuki, \q nayo huteketezwa kabisa kwa moto pale ilipo.
sw.R: Mtu yeyote anayeigusa \q anahitaji kifaa cha chuma au mpini wa mti wa mkuki. \q Huteketezwa kwa moto pale pale ilipo.

vi.L: Người nào đụng đến chúng \q phải trang bị [bằng] sắt và cán giáo, \q và chúng sẽ bị lửa thiêu sạch ngay tại chỗ.
vi.B: Ai muốn đụng đến chúng \q thì phải cầm đồ sắt hay cán giáo, \q và chúng bị lửa thiêu rụi ngay tại chỗ.
vi.R: Ai muốn đụng đến chúng \q thì phải có dụng cụ bằng sắt hay cán giáo bằng gỗ. \q Chúng bị đốt cháy trong lửa ngay tại chỗ.

decisions.choice: arms himself with iron and the shaft of a spear: uses a tool or weapon, never bare hands
decisions.reason: The verb is literally "is filled", here in the sense of being equipped. "Iron" may mean an iron tool or the spear's point; the wooden shaft would let a man rake the thorns into a pile without touching them.

decisions.choice: completely burned where they lie: burned up on the spot
alternatives: burned up until nothing is left
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis: "burning they will be burned". The last word usually means "sitting" or "dwelling", so "in their place", where they lie. Some take it from a similar root meaning "stopping", giving "burned up until nothing is left". The point is the same: the wicked are destroyed completely.

decisions.choice: Whoever (Balanced); Anyone (Readable); must be armed with
decisions.reason: The man is anyone at all who has to deal with thorns, so Balanced and Readable use words that include everyone, and Balanced says "be armed" for the reflexive "arms himself".

decisions.choice: {{gender:quiconque|l’homme qui}}
decisions.reason: The span holds the words French has to choose for the Hebrew "a man"; Balanced and Readable say "celui qui", which is already generic in French and takes no span (French style guide, section 7).

decisions.choice: el que los toca
decisions.reason: Spanish 'el que' already speaks of anyone, so the English gender span (anyone / a man) has no Spanish counterpart.

source.text: אֵ֛לֶּה שְׁמ֥וֹת הַגִּבֹּרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְדָוִ֑ד יֹשֵׁ֨ב בַּשֶּׁ֜בֶת תַּחְכְּמֹנִ֣י׀רֹ֣אשׁ הַשָּׁלִשִׁ֗י ה֚וּא עֲדִינ֣וֹ הָֽעֶצְנִ֔י עַל־שְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מֵא֛וֹת חָלָ֖ל בְּפַ֥עַם אֶחָֽת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: These [are the] names of the mighty men who [belonged] to David: Josheb-Basshebeth, a Tahchemonite, chief of the officers; he [was] Adino the Eznite, against eight hundred slain at one time.

en.L: These [are] the names of the mighty men whom David had: Josheb-Basshebeth, a Tahchemonite, chief of the officers; he [was] Adino the Eznite, [who was] against eight hundred slain at one time.
en.B: These are the names of David's mighty warriors. Josheb-Basshebeth the Tahchemonite was chief of the officers. He was also called Adino the Eznite, and he killed eight hundred men at one time.
en.R: Here are the names of David's best warriors. Josheb-Basshebeth the Tahchemonite was the leader of the officers. He was also called Adino the Eznite. In one battle he killed eight hundred men.

es.L: Estos [son] los nombres de los valientes que tenía David: Joseb-basebet, tacmonita, jefe de los oficiales; él [era] Adino el eznita, [que fue] contra ochocientos muertos de una vez.
es.B: Estos son los nombres de los guerreros valientes de David. Joseb-basebet el tacmonita era el jefe de los oficiales. También se le llamaba Adino el eznita, y mató a ochocientos hombres de una vez.
es.R: Estos son los nombres de los mejores guerreros de David. Joseb-basebet el tacmonita era el jefe de los oficiales. También lo llamaban Adino el eznita. En una sola batalla mató a ochocientos hombres.

fr.L: Voici les noms des vaillants hommes qu’avait David : Yosheb-Bashshébeth, le Tahkemonite, chef des officiers ; c’[était] Adino l’Etsnite, [qui fut] contre huit cents tués en une seule fois.
fr.B: Voici les noms des vaillants guerriers de David. Yosheb-Bashshébeth le Tahkemonite était le chef des officiers. On l’appelait aussi Adino l’Etsnite ; il tua huit cents hommes en une seule fois.
fr.R: Voici les noms des meilleurs guerriers de David. Yosheb-Bashshébeth le Tahkemonite était le chef des officiers. On l’appelait aussi Adino l’Etsnite. Dans une seule bataille, il a tué huit cents hommes.

sw.L: Haya [ndiyo] majina ya mashujaa aliokuwa nao Daudi: Yosheb-bashebethi, Mtakemoni, mkuu wa maafisa; yeye [ndiye] Adino Mwesni, [aliyepigana] dhidi ya watu mia nane waliouawa wakati mmoja.
sw.B: Haya ndiyo majina ya mashujaa wa Daudi. Yosheb-bashebethi Mtakemoni alikuwa mkuu wa maafisa. Aliitwa pia Adino Mwesni, naye aliwaua watu mia nane wakati mmoja.
sw.R: Haya ndiyo majina ya wapiganaji hodari kuliko wote wa Daudi. Yosheb-bashebethi Mtakemoni alikuwa kiongozi wa maafisa. Aliitwa pia Adino Mwesni. Katika vita kimoja aliwaua watu mia nane.

vi.L: Đây [là] tên của các dũng sĩ của Đa-vít: Giô-sép Ba-sê-bết, người Tác-kê-môn, đứng đầu các quan chỉ huy; ông [là] A-đi-nô người Ết-nít, [đã chống lại] tám trăm người bị giết trong một lần.
vi.B: Đây là tên các dũng sĩ của Đa-vít. Giô-sép Ba-sê-bết người Tác-kê-môn đứng đầu các quan chỉ huy. Ông còn được gọi là A-đi-nô người Ết-nít; ông đã giết tám trăm người trong một trận.
vi.R: Đây là tên những chiến binh giỏi nhất của Đa-vít. Giô-sép Ba-sê-bết người Tác-kê-môn là người đứng đầu các quan chỉ huy. Ông còn được gọi là A-đi-nô người Ết-nít. Trong một trận đánh, ông đã giết tám trăm người.

decisions.choice: the list of David's warriors: 1 Chronicles 11:10-41 is the parallel
decisions.reason: Chronicles gives the same list, placed at the start of David's reign, with many names spelled differently and sixteen more names at the end (1 Chronicles 11:41-47). The main differences are noted verse by verse.

decisions.choice: Josheb-Basshebeth the Tahchemonite ... Adino the Eznite ... eight hundred: the Hebrew text as it stands
alternatives: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni ... he raised his spear against three hundred (1 Chronicles 11:11)
decisions.reason: The verse is hard. The name Josheb-Basshebeth ("one who sits in the seat") may be a copying change from the name in 1 Chronicles 11:11, "Jashobeam son of Hachmoni". "He was Adino the Eznite" has no verb for the fighting; Chronicles reads instead "he raised his spear", and the Greek translation of Samuel has something similar. Chronicles also gives three hundred slain, not eight hundred (compare Abishai in verse 18). This translation follows the Hebrew of Samuel and supplies only what the sense needs.

decisions.choice: chief of the officers: the spoken reading; the written letters may mean "of the Three"
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew word and the scribes' reading differ slightly. One gives "the officers" (picked men who served close to the king, Exodus 14:7; 2 Kings 9:25), the other may be read "the Three", the small group named in verses 9-17. Chronicles has the same uncertainty (1 Chronicles 11:11). Either way he was the first of David's warriors.

decisions.choice: mighty warriors (Balanced); best warriors (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word is the plural of "mighty man", a hero or champion in battle. Literal keeps "mighty men"; Balanced says "mighty warriors", as in 16:6, and Readable "best warriors". The same wording is used through the chapter.

decisions.choice: he killed eight hundred men
decisions.reason: "Against eight hundred slain" means he fought them and they fell by his hand, so Balanced and Readable supply the verb "killed". Readable also says "also called" to show that Adino the Eznite names the same man.

decisions.choice: names of the list (verses 8-39) in French transcription: "sh", "ts", "k", "ou", "gu", "y" for the Hebrew sounds
decisions.reason: The list of David’s warriors follows one set of French spellings, as the Samuel terms note does for its names; names already published keep their form (Joab, Asahel, Urie le Hittite, Ahitofel, Ittaï).

decisions.choice: los valientes (L); los guerreros valientes (B); los mejores guerreros (R); the names of the list as usual Spanish forms
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the one for mighty fighting men; Literal says 'los valientes', Balanced and Readable follow the English 'mighty warriors' and 'best warriors'. The names in verses 8-39 take their usual Spanish spelling, with Spanish gentilics (el tacmonita, el harodita, el netofatita).

decisions.choice: Yosheb-bashebethi Mtakemoni; Adino Mwesni
decisions.reason: The names of David's warriors in verses 8-39 follow the usual Swahili pattern, ending in a vowel; a man of a clan or place takes the prefix "M-" or "Mw-" (Mtakemoni, Mharodi, Mnetofathi), as "Mgiti" and "Mgiloni" earlier in this block.

decisions.choice: "Giô-sép Ba-sê-bết", "người Tác-kê-môn", "A-đi-nô người Ết-nít"
decisions.reason: The list of David's warriors keeps the usual Vietnamese forms of each name; the names in verses 8-39 follow the same pattern and are kept through Samuel and Chronicles.

source.text: וְאַחֲרָ֛יו אֶלְעָזָ֥ר בֶּן־דֹּד֖וֹ בֶּן־אֲחֹחִ֑י בִּשְׁלֹשָׁ֨ה הַגִּבֹּרִ֜ים עִם־דָּוִ֗ד בְּחָֽרְפָ֤ם בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּים נֶאֶסְפוּ־שָׁ֣ם לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וַֽיַּעֲל֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And after him Eleazar son of Dodo son of Ahohite, among [the] three mighty men with David when they taunted among [the] Philistines [who] were gathered there for battle; and went up [the] men of Israel.

en.L: And after him [was] Eleazar son of Dodo, son of an Ahohite, among the three mighty men with David when they taunted the Philistines [who] were gathered there for battle, and the men of Israel went up.
en.B: Next to him was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite. He was one of the three mighty warriors with David when they defied the Philistines who had gathered there for battle, and the men of Israel withdrew.
en.R: Next came Eleazar son of Dodo from the clan of Ahoah. He was one of the three best warriors who were with David when they dared the Philistines to fight. The Philistines had gathered there for battle, and the rest of Israel's soldiers pulled back.

es.L: Y después de él [estaba] Eleazar hijo de Dodo, hijo de un ahohíta, entre los tres valientes que estaban con David cuando desafiaron a los filisteos [que] se habían reunido allí para la batalla, y los hombres de Israel se retiraron.
es.B: Después de él venía Eleazar hijo de Dodo el ahohíta. Era uno de los tres guerreros valientes que estaban con David cuando desafiaron a los filisteos que se habían reunido allí para la batalla, y los hombres de Israel se retiraron.
es.R: Después venía Eleazar hijo de Dodo, del clan de Ahoa. Era uno de los tres mejores guerreros que estaban con David cuando desafiaron a los filisteos a pelear. Los filisteos se habían reunido allí para la batalla, y el resto de los soldados de Israel se retiró.

fr.L: Et après lui [venait] Éléazar, fils de Dodo, fils d’un Ahohite, parmi les trois vaillants hommes avec David quand ils défièrent les Philistins [qui] s’étaient rassemblés là pour le combat ; et les hommes d’Israël montèrent.
fr.B: Après lui venait Éléazar, fils de Dodo l’Ahohite. Il était l’un des trois vaillants guerriers qui étaient avec David quand ils défièrent les Philistins rassemblés là pour le combat, alors que les hommes d’Israël se retiraient.
fr.R: Ensuite venait Éléazar, fils de Dodo, du clan d’Ahoah. C’était l’un des trois meilleurs guerriers qui étaient avec David quand ils ont provoqué les Philistins. Les Philistins s’étaient rassemblés là pour combattre, et le reste des soldats d’Israël a reculé.

sw.L: Na baada yake [alikuwa] Eleazari mwana wa Dodo, mwana wa Mwahohi, mmoja wa mashujaa watatu waliokuwa pamoja na Daudi walipowadhihaki Wafilisti [waliokuwa] wamekusanyika huko kwa vita, na watu wa Israeli wakapanda.
sw.B: Aliyefuata baada yake alikuwa Eleazari mwana wa Dodo Mwahohi. Yeye alikuwa mmoja wa mashujaa watatu waliokuwa pamoja na Daudi walipowatukana Wafilisti waliokuwa wamekusanyika huko kwa vita, nao watu wa Israeli wakarudi nyuma.
sw.R: Aliyefuata alikuwa Eleazari mwana wa Dodo, wa ukoo wa Ahohi. Yeye alikuwa mmoja wa wale wapiganaji watatu hodari kuliko wote waliokuwa pamoja na Daudi walipowachokoza Wafilisti wapigane nao. Wafilisti walikuwa wamekusanyika huko kwa vita, na askari wengine wa Israeli wakarudi nyuma.

vi.L: Sau ông [là] Ê-lê-a-xa con trai Đô-đô, con một người A-hô-a, một trong ba dũng sĩ ở với Đa-vít khi họ thách thức người Phi-li-tin [đã] tập hợp ở đó để giao chiến, và người Y-sơ-ra-ên rút lên.
vi.B: Kế đến là Ê-lê-a-xa con trai Đô-đô người A-hô-a. Ông là một trong ba dũng sĩ ở với Đa-vít khi họ thách thức quân Phi-li-tin đang tập hợp ở đó để giao chiến, trong khi người Y-sơ-ra-ên rút lui.
vi.R: Kế đến là Ê-lê-a-xa con trai Đô-đô, thuộc dòng họ A-hô-a. Ông là một trong ba chiến binh giỏi nhất ở với Đa-vít khi họ thách quân Phi-li-tin ra đánh. Quân Phi-li-tin đã tập hợp ở đó để giao chiến, còn những binh sĩ khác của Y-sơ-ra-ên thì rút lui.

decisions.choice: the three mighty men: a small group, the Three, who stood above all of David's other warriors
decisions.reason: Josheb-Basshebeth (verse 8), Eleazar (verses 9-10) and Shammah (verses 11-12) are the Three. Below them stood the larger group called the Thirty (verses 13, 18-24).

decisions.choice: when they taunted the Philistines: Chronicles names the place, Pas-dammim
alternatives: he was with David at Pas-dammim (1 Chronicles 11:13)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is unusual: "when they taunted among the Philistines". The parallel in 1 Chronicles 11:13 reads "he was with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines gathered there", and "there" in this verse suggests that a place name once stood here too. Pas-dammim is where the Philistines camped when David fought Goliath (1 Samuel 17:1, Ephes-dammim). The sense of the Hebrew of Samuel is kept.

decisions.choice: the men of Israel went up: Israel's army pulled back
decisions.reason: "Went up" here means went away from the battle, probably up into the hills, leaving Eleazar to fight (compare 1 Samuel 14:46). Verse 10 shows they came back only after the fighting was over.

decisions.choice: from the clan of Ahoah
decisions.reason: "Son of an Ahohite" means he belonged to the family of Ahoah, a descendant of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:4). Readable says this in plain words; Balanced uses the usual form "the Ahohite".

source.text: ה֣וּא קָם֩ וַיַּ֨ךְ בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֜ים עַ֣ד׀כִּֽי־יָגְעָ֣ה יָד֗וֹ וַתִּדְבַּ֤ק יָדוֹ֙ אֶל־הַחֶ֔רֶב וַיַּ֧עַשׂ יְהוָ֛ה תְּשׁוּעָ֥ה גְדוֹלָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְהָעָ֛ם יָשֻׁ֥בוּ אַחֲרָ֖יו אַךְ־לְפַשֵּֽׁט׃ס

records.literal_gloss: He arose and struck among [the] Philistines until that was weary his hand, and clung his hand to the sword; and did Yahweh a victory great on the day the that; and the people, they returned after him only to strip.

en.L: He arose and struck down Philistines until his hand was weary and his hand clung to the sword; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} worked a great victory on that day, and the people returned after him only to strip [the slain].
en.B: He stood his ground and struck down Philistines until his hand grew tired and stuck fast to his sword. On that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} won a great victory, and the troops came back to him only to strip the dead.
en.R: But Eleazar stood and fought the Philistines until his hand was so tired that it stuck to his sword. That day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Israel a great victory. The army came back to Eleazar only to take things from the dead bodies.

es.L: Él se levantó e hirió a los filisteos hasta que su mano se cansó y su mano se quedó pegada a la espada; y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} obró una gran victoria aquel día, y el pueblo volvió tras él solo para despojar [a los muertos].
es.B: Él se mantuvo firme e hirió a los filisteos hasta que la mano se le cansó y se le quedó pegada a la espada. Aquel día {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} obtuvo una gran victoria, y la tropa volvió adonde él estaba solo para despojar a los muertos.
es.R: Pero Eleazar se quedó y peleó contra los filisteos hasta que tenía la mano tan cansada que se le quedó pegada a la espada. Ese día {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio a Israel una gran victoria. El ejército volvió adonde estaba Eleazar solo para quitarles las cosas a los muertos.

fr.L: Il se leva et frappa les Philistins jusqu’à ce que sa main fût lasse et que sa main restât attachée à l’épée ; et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} opéra une grande victoire ce jour-là, et le peuple revint derrière lui seulement pour dépouiller [les morts].
fr.B: Il tint bon et frappa les Philistins jusqu’à ce que sa main, épuisée, reste collée à son épée. Ce jour-là, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} remporta une grande victoire, et la troupe ne revint vers lui que pour dépouiller les morts.
fr.R: Mais Éléazar est resté là et il a combattu les Philistins jusqu’à ce que sa main soit si fatiguée qu’elle est restée collée à son épée. Ce jour-là, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné une grande victoire à Israël. L’armée est revenue vers Éléazar seulement pour prendre les affaires des morts.

sw.L: Akainuka akawapiga Wafilisti hata mkono wake ukachoka, na mkono wake ukaganda kwenye upanga; na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akatenda ushindi mkuu siku ile, na watu wakarudi nyuma yake ili kuteka nyara tu.
sw.B: Akasimama imara, akawapiga Wafilisti mpaka mkono wake ukachoka na kugandamana na upanga wake. Siku ile {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alileta ushindi mkuu, na askari wakarudi kwake ili kuwavua wafu tu.
sw.R: Lakini Eleazari akasimama, akapigana na Wafilisti mpaka mkono wake ukachoka hata ukashikamana na upanga wake. Siku ile {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwapa Israeli ushindi mkuu. Jeshi likarudi kwa Eleazari ili tu kuchukua vitu kutoka kwa maiti.

vi.L: Ông đứng dậy đánh giết người Phi-li-tin cho đến khi tay ông mỏi và tay ông dính chặt vào gươm. Ngày ấy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} làm nên một chiến thắng lớn, và dân chúng trở lại theo ông chỉ để lột [đồ người chết].
vi.B: Ông đứng vững và đánh giết quân Phi-li-tin cho đến khi tay mỏi nhừ và dính chặt vào thanh gươm. Ngày ấy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã ban một chiến thắng lớn, và quân lính trở lại với ông chỉ để lột đồ người chết.
vi.R: Nhưng Ê-lê-a-xa đứng lại đánh quân Phi-li-tin cho đến khi tay ông mỏi đến nỗi dính chặt vào thanh gươm. Ngày ấy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã ban cho Y-sơ-ra-ên một chiến thắng lớn. Đạo quân quay lại với Ê-lê-a-xa chỉ để lấy đồ của những người chết.

decisions.choice: his hand grew weary and clung to the sword: he fought so long his hand cramped around the hilt
decisions.reason: The picture is of a fighter whose grip has locked from long effort, so that hand and sword seem joined.

decisions.choice: Yahweh worked a great victory: the victory is God's, though Eleazar fought
decisions.reason: The noun means rescue or deliverance, here won in battle. The narrator credits it to Yahweh, as Jonathan does in 1 Samuel 14:6 and David in 1 Samuel 17:47. The same words come again for Shammah in verse 12.

decisions.choice: the people returned only to strip: the army came back after the fighting to take spoil
decisions.reason: "The people" here is the army. Soldiers took weapons, armor and goods from the bodies of fallen enemies (1 Samuel 31:8). The troops who had pulled back (verse 9) returned only when there was nothing left to do but gather the spoil.

decisions.choice: the people (Literal); the troops (Balanced); the army (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word for "people" here means the army in the field, so Balanced says "troops" and Readable "army", as elsewhere in these books.

source.text: וְאַחֲרָ֛יו שַׁמָּ֥א בֶן־אָגֵ֖א הָרָרִ֑י וַיֵּאָסְפ֨וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֜ים לַחַיָּ֗ה וַתְּהִי־שָׁ֞ם חֶלְקַ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ מְלֵאָ֣ה עֲדָשִׁ֔ים וְהָעָ֥ם נָ֖ס מִפְּנֵ֥י פְלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And after him Shammah son of Agee [the] Hararite; and gathered [the] Philistines to the troop, and was there a plot of the field full [of] lentils, and the people fled from before [the] Philistines.

en.L: And after him [was] Shammah son of Agee [the] Hararite. And [the] Philistines gathered into a troop, and there was there a plot of the field full of lentils; and the people fled before [the] Philistines.
en.B: Next to him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines had massed in a troop where a plot of land was full of lentils, and the troops ran from the Philistines.
en.R: Next came Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines had gathered their soldiers in one place. There was a field there full of lentils, and the army of Israel ran away from the Philistines.

es.L: Y después de él [estaba] Sama hijo de Age el ararita. Y los filisteos se juntaron en tropa, y había allí una parcela del campo llena de lentejas; y el pueblo huyó delante de los filisteos.
es.B: Después de él venía Sama hijo de Age el ararita. Los filisteos se habían agrupado en tropa donde había una parcela llena de lentejas, y la tropa huyó delante de los filisteos.
es.R: Después venía Sama hijo de Age el ararita. Los filisteos habían reunido a sus soldados en un lugar donde había un campo lleno de lentejas, y el ejército de Israel huyó de los filisteos.

fr.L: Et après lui [venait] Shamma, fils d’Agué, le Hararite. Et les Philistins se rassemblèrent en troupe, et il y avait là une parcelle de champ pleine de lentilles ; et le peuple s’enfuit devant les Philistins.
fr.B: Après lui venait Shamma, fils d’Agué le Hararite. Les Philistins s’étaient rassemblés en troupe à un endroit où il y avait une parcelle pleine de lentilles, et la troupe s’enfuit devant les Philistins.
fr.R: Ensuite venait Shamma, fils d’Agué le Hararite. Les Philistins avaient rassemblé leurs soldats en un seul endroit. Il y avait là un champ plein de lentilles, et l’armée d’Israël s’est enfuie devant les Philistins.

sw.L: Na baada yake [alikuwa] Shama mwana wa Age Mharari. Wafilisti wakakusanyika kuwa kikosi, na huko palikuwa na kipande cha shamba kilichojaa dengu; na watu wakakimbia mbele ya Wafilisti.
sw.B: Aliyefuata baada yake alikuwa Shama mwana wa Age Mharari. Wafilisti walikuwa wamekusanyika kikosi mahali palipokuwa na kipande cha shamba kilichojaa dengu, na askari wakawakimbia Wafilisti.
sw.R: Aliyefuata alikuwa Shama mwana wa Age Mharari. Wafilisti walikuwa wamekusanya askari wao mahali pamoja. Huko palikuwa na shamba lililojaa dengu, na jeshi la Israeli likawakimbia Wafilisti.

vi.L: Sau ông [là] Sam-ma con trai A-ghê người Ha-ra. Người Phi-li-tin tập hợp thành một toán, và ở đó có một thửa ruộng đầy đậu lăng; dân chúng chạy trốn trước mặt người Phi-li-tin.
vi.B: Kế đến là Sam-ma con trai A-ghê người Ha-ra. Quân Phi-li-tin tập hợp thành một toán tại nơi có một thửa ruộng đầy đậu lăng, và quân lính chạy trốn trước mặt người Phi-li-tin.
vi.R: Kế đến là Sam-ma con trai A-ghê người Ha-ra. Quân Phi-li-tin đã tập hợp binh lính tại một nơi. Ở đó có một thửa ruộng đầy đậu lăng, và quân Y-sơ-ra-ên bỏ chạy trước mặt quân Phi-li-tin.

decisions.choice: gathered into a troop: the Philistines massed together; or, gathered at Lehi
decisions.reason: The word is used of a band or company in verse 13 and in Psalm 68:11. With different vowels it is the place name Lehi, where Samson fought the Philistines (Judges 15:9, 14), and some read "gathered at Lehi". The written consonants allow both; the vowels of the Hebrew text give "troop".

decisions.choice: Shammah and the field of lentils: in Chronicles the story is told of Eleazar, in a field of barley
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 11:13-14 has no Shammah. It joins the field story to Eleazar at Pas-dammim and says the field was full of barley. The Samuel text names three heroes, each with his own exploit.

decisions.choice: a plot full of lentils: a crop the Philistines had come to plunder
decisions.reason: Lentils were a common food crop (Genesis 25:34; 2 Samuel 17:28). Raiders often came at harvest to take or burn the crops (Judges 6:3-4; 15:5), so Shammah was defending the food of his people.

decisions.choice: the people (Literal); the troops (Balanced); the army of Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, "people" here is Israel's army.

source.text: וַיִּתְיַצֵּ֤ב בְּתוֹךְ־הַֽחֶלְקָה֙ וַיַּצִּילֶ֔הָ וַיַּ֖ךְ אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ יְהוָ֖ה תְּשׁוּעָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he stationed himself in [the] middle of the plot and delivered it and struck down Philistines; and did Yahweh a victory great.

en.L: And he took his stand in [the] middle of the plot and rescued it and struck down [the] Philistines; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} worked a great victory.
en.B: But he took his stand in the middle of the plot, defended it and struck down the Philistines, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} won a great victory.
en.R: But Shammah stood in the middle of the field and kept the Philistines from taking it. He killed the Philistines, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Israel a great victory.

es.L: Y él se plantó en medio de la parcela y la defendió, e hirió a los filisteos; y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} obró una gran victoria.
es.B: Pero él se plantó en medio de la parcela, la defendió e hirió a los filisteos, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} obtuvo una gran victoria.
es.R: Pero Sama se quedó en medio del campo y no dejó que los filisteos lo tomaran. Mató a los filisteos, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio a Israel una gran victoria.

fr.L: Et il se posta au milieu de la parcelle, et la délivra, et frappa les Philistins ; et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} opéra une grande victoire.
fr.B: Mais lui se posta au milieu de la parcelle, la défendit et frappa les Philistins, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} remporta une grande victoire.
fr.R: Mais Shamma s’est tenu au milieu du champ et il a empêché les Philistins de le prendre. Il a tué les Philistins, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné une grande victoire à Israël.

sw.L: Akasimama katikati ya kipande hicho akakiokoa, akawapiga Wafilisti; na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akatenda ushindi mkuu.
sw.B: Lakini yeye akasimama imara katikati ya shamba hilo, akalilinda, akawapiga Wafilisti, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaleta ushindi mkuu.
sw.R: Lakini Shama akasimama katikati ya shamba hilo, akawazuia Wafilisti wasilichukue. Akawaua Wafilisti, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawapa Israeli ushindi mkuu.

vi.L: Ông đứng giữa thửa ruộng, giải cứu nó, và đánh giết người Phi-li-tin; và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} làm nên một chiến thắng lớn.
vi.B: Nhưng ông đứng vững giữa thửa ruộng, bảo vệ nó và đánh giết quân Phi-li-tin, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã ban một chiến thắng lớn.
vi.R: Nhưng Sam-ma đứng giữa thửa ruộng và không để quân Phi-li-tin chiếm lấy nó. Ông giết quân Phi-li-tin, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã ban cho Y-sơ-ra-ên một chiến thắng lớn.

decisions.choice: took his stand ... rescued it: he held his ground and saved the field from the enemy
decisions.reason: The verb "took his stand" is used of a fighter who stays in place when others flee. "Rescued it" refers to the plot of ground: he kept it from being plundered.

decisions.choice: Yahweh worked a great victory: as in verse 10
decisions.reason: The same words as in verse 10 credit Yahweh with the victory. 1 Chronicles 11:14 has the verbs in the plural, "they took their stand ... and they struck down", since there both David and Eleazar are present.

decisions.choice: gave Israel a great victory
decisions.reason: Readable says for whom the victory was won, which the context makes clear, and names Shammah to keep the subject plain.

source.text: וַיֵּרְד֨וּ שְׁלֹשָׁ֜ה מֵהַשְּׁלֹשִׁ֣ים רֹ֗אשׁ וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ אֶל־קָצִיר֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד אֶל־מְעָרַ֖ת עֲדֻלָּ֑ם וְחַיַּ֣ת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים חֹנָ֖ה בְּעֵ֥מֶק רְפָאִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And went down three of the thirty chief and came to harvest to David to [the] cave of Adullam; and a troop of Philistines [was] encamping in [the] Valley of Rephaim.

en.L: And three of the Thirty, chiefs, went down and came at harvest to David, to the cave of Adullam, and a troop of [the] Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.
en.B: Once, at harvest time, three chief men of the Thirty went down and joined David at the cave of Adullam, while a band of Philistines was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
en.R: One time, during the harvest, three leaders from the Thirty went down to join David at the cave of Adullam. A group of Philistine soldiers was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.

es.L: Y tres de los Treinta, jefes, descendieron y vinieron en la siega a David, a la cueva de Adulam; y una tropa de filisteos estaba acampada en el valle de Refaim.
es.B: Una vez, en tiempo de la siega, tres de los jefes de los Treinta bajaron y se unieron a David en la cueva de Adulam, mientras una banda de filisteos acampaba en el valle de Refaim.
es.R: Una vez, durante la cosecha, tres líderes de los Treinta bajaron a reunirse con David en la cueva de Adulam. Un grupo de soldados filisteos estaba acampado en el valle de Refaim.

fr.L: Et trois des Trente, des chefs, descendirent et vinrent, au temps de la moisson, vers David, à la caverne d’Adoullam ; et une troupe de Philistins campait dans la vallée des Rephaïm.
fr.B: Un jour, au temps de la moisson, trois des chefs des Trente descendirent rejoindre David à la caverne d’Adoullam, pendant qu’une troupe de Philistins campait dans la vallée des Rephaïm.
fr.R: Une fois, pendant la moisson, trois chefs du groupe des Trente sont descendus rejoindre David à la caverne d’Adoullam. Un groupe de soldats philistins campait dans la vallée des Rephaïm.

sw.L: Watatu wa wale Thelathini, wakuu, wakashuka wakaja wakati wa mavuno kwa Daudi, kwenye pango la Adulamu, na kikosi cha Wafilisti kilikuwa kimepiga kambi katika Bonde la Refaimu.
sw.B: Wakati mmoja, wakati wa mavuno, wakuu watatu wa wale Thelathini walishuka wakajiunga na Daudi kwenye pango la Adulamu, wakati kikosi cha Wafilisti kilipokuwa kimepiga kambi katika Bonde la Refaimu.
sw.R: Wakati mmoja, wakati wa mavuno, viongozi watatu kutoka wale Thelathini walishuka kujiunga na Daudi kwenye pango la Adulamu. Kundi la askari wa Kifilisti lilikuwa limepiga kambi katika Bonde la Refaimu.

vi.L: Ba người trong nhóm Ba Mươi, là những người đứng đầu, đi xuống đến với Đa-vít vào mùa gặt, tại hang A-đu-lam, trong khi một toán quân Phi-li-tin đóng trại trong thung lũng Rê-pha-im.
vi.B: Có lần, vào mùa gặt, ba người đứng đầu trong nhóm Ba Mươi đi xuống gặp Đa-vít tại hang A-đu-lam, trong khi một toán quân Phi-li-tin đóng trại trong thung lũng Rê-pha-im.
vi.R: Có một lần, vào mùa gặt, ba người lãnh đạo trong nhóm Ba Mươi đi xuống gặp Đa-vít tại hang A-đu-lam. Một toán lính Phi-li-tin đang đóng trại trong thung lũng Rê-pha-im.

decisions.choice: three of the thirty chiefs: the spoken reading gives "three"; the written letters "thirty"
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has "thirty" twice, which the scribes' reading corrects to "three of the thirty". These three are not named. They may be the Three of verses 8-12 or three other men from the Thirty; verse 17 calls them "the three mighty men".

decisions.choice: at harvest: Chronicles has "to the rock"
alternatives: went down to the rock to David (1 Chronicles 11:15)
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 11:15 reads "to the rock" where Samuel has "to harvest"; the two Hebrew words look alike. The sense of Samuel is kept: it was harvest time, the season when raids on crops were common (verse 11).

decisions.choice: the cave of Adullam; the Valley of Rephaim
decisions.reason: Adullam lay in the hill country southwest of Bethlehem; David hid in a cave there when he fled from Saul (1 Samuel 22:1). The Valley of Rephaim runs southwest from Jerusalem toward Bethlehem; the Philistines came up into it in 5:18, 22. The story may belong to the time of those battles or to David's years as a fugitive.

decisions.choice: Once, at harvest time
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the time first and add "once" to show that a new story begins, which the Hebrew shows by its change of subject.

decisions.choice: los Tres; los Treinta
decisions.reason: As the English, the names of David's two companies of warriors take capitals, so that readers see them as groups with a rank and not plain numbers.

decisions.choice: wale Thelathini; wale Watatu
decisions.reason: The two bands of warriors are named groups, so Swahili writes them with capitals, "wale Watatu" and "wale Thelathini", as the English writes "the Three" and "the Thirty".

decisions.choice: "nhóm Ba Mươi" and "nhóm Ba" for the Thirty and the Three
decisions.reason: Where the number names a group, Vietnamese adds "nhóm" and capitalises the number, as the English capitalises "the Thirty" and "the Three".

source.text: וְדָוִ֖ד אָ֣ז בַּמְּצוּדָ֑ה וּמַצַּ֣ב פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים אָ֖ז בֵּ֥ית לָֽחֶם׃

records.literal_gloss: And David then [was] in the stronghold, and [the] garrison of [the] Philistines then [was in] Bethlehem.

en.L: And David [was] then in the stronghold, and [the] garrison of [the] Philistines [was] then [in] Bethlehem.
en.B: At that time David was in the stronghold, and a Philistine garrison was then in Bethlehem.
en.R: At that time David was in his hiding place in the hills, and a group of Philistine soldiers was holding Bethlehem.

es.L: Y David [estaba] entonces en la fortaleza, y la guarnición de los filisteos [estaba] entonces [en] Belén.
es.B: En aquel tiempo David estaba en la fortaleza, y había una guarnición filistea en Belén.
es.R: En aquel tiempo David estaba en su escondite en los montes, y un grupo de soldados filisteos ocupaba Belén.

fr.L: Et David [était] alors dans la forteresse, et le poste des Philistins [était] alors [à] Bethléem.
fr.B: David était alors dans la forteresse, et un poste philistin se trouvait alors à Bethléem.
fr.R: À ce moment-là, David était dans sa cachette dans les collines, et un groupe de soldats philistins occupait Bethléem.

sw.L: Daudi [alikuwa] wakati huo ngomeni, na kambi ya Wafilisti [ilikuwa] wakati huo [huko] Bethlehemu.
sw.B: Wakati huo Daudi alikuwa ngomeni, na kikosi cha askari wa Kifilisti kilikuwa Bethlehemu.
sw.R: Wakati huo Daudi alikuwa mahali pake pa kujificha milimani, na kundi la askari wa Kifilisti lilikuwa limeushika mji wa Bethlehemu.

vi.L: Lúc ấy Đa-vít [ở] trong đồn, còn đồn binh của người Phi-li-tin lúc ấy [ở] Bết-lê-hem.
vi.B: Lúc ấy Đa-vít đang ở trong đồn, còn một đồn binh Phi-li-tin thì đóng ở Bết-lê-hem.
vi.R: Lúc ấy Đa-vít đang ở nơi ẩn náu trên vùng đồi núi, còn một toán lính Phi-li-tin đang chiếm giữ Bết-lê-hem.

decisions.choice: the stronghold: a natural fortress in the rocky country, probably near Adullam
decisions.reason: The same word is used of David's refuges when he hid from Saul (1 Samuel 22:4-5; 24:23) and of the stronghold he went down to in 5:17. Here it is linked with the cave of Adullam (verse 13).

decisions.choice: a Philistine garrison in Bethlehem: an enemy post in David's home town
decisions.reason: Bethlehem was David's birthplace (1 Samuel 16:1; 17:12). The Philistines held posts inside Israel's land to control it (1 Samuel 10:5; 13:23). So the town David longed for was in enemy hands.

decisions.choice: his hiding place in the hills
decisions.reason: Readable explains "stronghold", which here is not a built fort but a place of refuge in rough country.

source.text: וַיִּתְאַוֶּ֥ה דָוִ֖ד וַיֹּאמַ֑ר מִ֚י יַשְׁקֵ֣נִי מַ֔יִם מִבֹּ֥אר בֵּֽית־לֶ֖חֶם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּשָּֽׁעַר׃

records.literal_gloss: And longed David and said, Who will give me drink water from [the] well of Bethlehem which [is] at the gate?

en.L: And David longed and said, "Who will give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem that [is] by the gate?"
en.B: David had a longing and said, "If only someone would get me water to drink from Bethlehem's well, the one by the gate!"
en.R: David felt homesick and said, "I wish someone would bring me water from the well by Bethlehem's gate!"

es.L: Y David tuvo un deseo y dijo: «¿Quién me dará a beber agua del pozo de Belén que [está] junto a la puerta?».
es.B: David sintió un antojo y dijo: «¡Si alguien me trajera de beber agua del pozo de Belén, el que está junto a la puerta!».
es.R: David sintió nostalgia y dijo: «¡Cómo quisiera que alguien me trajera agua del pozo que está junto a la puerta de Belén!».

fr.L: Et David eut un désir et dit : « Qui me fera boire de l’eau du puits de Bethléem qui [est] près de la porte ? »
fr.B: David fut pris d’un désir et dit : « Si seulement quelqu’un me faisait boire de l’eau du puits de Bethléem, celui qui est près de la porte ! »
fr.R: David avait le mal du pays, et il a dit : « J’aimerais tant que quelqu’un m’apporte de l’eau du puits qui est près de la porte de Bethléem ! »

sw.L: Daudi akatamani akasema, "Nani atanipa maji ya kunywa kutoka kisima cha Bethlehemu kilicho karibu na lango?"
sw.B: Daudi akatamani akasema, "Laiti mtu angeniletea maji ya kunywa kutoka kisima cha Bethlehemu, kile kilicho karibu na lango!"
sw.R: Daudi akakumbuka nyumbani kwao kwa hamu, akasema, "Natamani mtu aniletee maji kutoka kisima kilicho karibu na lango la Bethlehemu!"

vi.L: Đa-vít khao khát và nói: "Ai sẽ cho tôi uống nước từ giếng Bết-lê-hem ở bên cổng thành?"
vi.B: Đa-vít khao khát và nói: "Ước gì có ai lấy cho tôi nước từ giếng Bết-lê-hem, cái giếng bên cổng thành, để uống!"
vi.R: Đa-vít nhớ quê và nói: "Ước gì có ai đem cho tôi nước từ cái giếng bên cổng thành Bết-lê-hem!"

decisions.choice: who will give me water to drink? a wish, not a command
decisions.reason: "Who will ...?" is a common Hebrew way of saying "if only" (Numbers 11:4; Psalm 55:7). David speaks of a longing for the water of his home town; he does not order anyone to go.

decisions.choice: If only someone would (Balanced); I wish someone would (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the question into the wish it expresses. Readable says "homesick" for "longed", since the water is from his home town.

source.text: וַיִּבְקְעוּ֩ שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת הַגִּבֹּרִ֜ים בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיִּֽשְׁאֲבוּ־מַ֨יִם֙ מִבֹּ֤אר בֵּֽית־לֶ֨חֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשַּׁ֔עַר וַיִּשְׂא֖וּ וַיָּבִ֣אוּ אֶל־דָּוִ֑ד וְלֹ֤א אָבָה֙ לִשְׁתּוֹתָ֔ם וַיַּסֵּ֥ךְ אֹתָ֖ם לַֽיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And broke through [the] three of the mighty men into [the] camp of [the] Philistines, and drew water from [the] well of Bethlehem which [was] at the gate, and carried and brought to David; and not was willing to drink them, and he poured them out to Yahweh.

en.L: And the three mighty men broke through into the camp of [the] Philistines and drew water from the well of Bethlehem that [was] by the gate, and carried [it] and brought [it] to David. But he was not willing to drink it, and he poured it out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: So the three mighty warriors broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well of Bethlehem by the gate, and carried it back to David. But he would not drink it. Instead he poured it out as an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: So the three best warriors forced their way through the Philistine camp. They got water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem and carried it back to David. But David refused to drink it. Instead he poured it out on the ground as a gift to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y los tres valientes irrumpieron en el campamento de los filisteos y sacaron agua del pozo de Belén que [estaba] junto a la puerta, y [la] tomaron y [la] trajeron a David. Pero él no quiso beberla, y la derramó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.B: Entonces los tres guerreros valientes se abrieron paso a través del campamento filisteo, sacaron agua del pozo de Belén que está junto a la puerta y se la llevaron a David. Pero él no quiso beberla, sino que la derramó como ofrenda {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.R: Entonces los tres mejores guerreros pasaron a la fuerza por el campamento de los filisteos. Sacaron agua del pozo que está junto a la puerta de Belén y se la llevaron a David. Pero David no quiso beberla. En cambio, la derramó en el suelo como un regalo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et les trois vaillants hommes forcèrent l’entrée du camp des Philistins, et puisèrent de l’eau du puits de Bethléem qui [était] près de la porte, et [l’]emportèrent et [l’]apportèrent à David. Mais il ne voulut pas la boire, et il la répandit pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Les trois vaillants guerriers traversèrent donc de force le camp des Philistins, puisèrent de l’eau au puits de Bethléem, près de la porte, et la rapportèrent à David. Mais il ne voulut pas la boire. Il la répandit plutôt en offrande {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Alors les trois meilleurs guerriers sont passés de force à travers le camp des Philistins. Ils ont puisé de l’eau au puits près de la porte de Bethléem et ils l’ont rapportée à David. Mais David a refusé de la boire. Il l’a plutôt versée par terre, comme un cadeau {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Wale mashujaa watatu wakapenya katika kambi ya Wafilisti, wakateka maji kutoka kisima cha Bethlehemu kilichokuwa karibu na lango, wakayachukua wakamletea Daudi. Lakini hakukubali kuyanywa, akayamimina kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Basi wale mashujaa watatu wakapenya kambi ya Wafilisti, wakateka maji kutoka kisima cha Bethlehemu kilichokuwa karibu na lango, wakamletea Daudi. Lakini hakukubali kuyanywa. Badala yake akayamimina kuwa sadaka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Basi wale wapiganaji watatu hodari wakapita kwa nguvu katikati ya kambi ya Wafilisti. Wakachota maji kutoka kisima kilicho karibu na lango la Bethlehemu, wakamletea Daudi. Lakini Daudi akakataa kuyanywa. Badala yake akayamwaga chini kuwa zawadi kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Ba dũng sĩ phá vòng vây xông vào trại quân Phi-li-tin, múc nước từ giếng Bết-lê-hem ở bên cổng thành, mang đến cho Đa-vít. Nhưng ông không chịu uống, và ông đổ nước ra dâng cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Vậy ba dũng sĩ xông qua trại quân Phi-li-tin, múc nước từ giếng Bết-lê-hem bên cổng thành rồi mang về cho Đa-vít. Nhưng ông không chịu uống. Thay vào đó, ông đổ nước ra làm lễ dâng lên {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Vậy ba chiến binh giỏi nhất liều mình xông qua trại quân Phi-li-tin. Họ lấy nước từ cái giếng gần cổng thành Bết-lê-hem và mang về cho Đa-vít. Nhưng Đa-vít không chịu uống. Thay vào đó, ông đổ nước xuống đất như một món quà dâng lên {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

decisions.choice: broke through into the camp: forced their way through the enemy lines
decisions.reason: The verb means to split or break open. The three men cut their way through the Philistine positions to reach the well and came back the same way.

decisions.choice: poured it out to Yahweh: a drink offering
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for pouring out a drink offering (Genesis 35:14; Numbers 28:7). David treats the water as too precious for himself and gives it to God instead (compare 1 Samuel 7:6). Verse 17 gives his reason.

decisions.choice: 1 Chronicles 11:17-19 tells the same story
decisions.reason: Chronicles gives verses 15-17 almost word for word.

decisions.choice: as an offering (Balanced); on the ground as a gift (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what pouring out to the LORD was, an offering, so it does not read as wasting the water.

source.text: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר חָלִילָה֩ לִּ֨י יְהוָ֜ה מֵעֲשֹׂ֣תִי זֹ֗את הֲדַ֤ם הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ הַהֹלְכִ֣ים בְּנַפְשׁוֹתָ֔ם וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לִשְׁתּוֹתָ֑ם אֵ֣לֶּה עָשׂ֔וּ שְׁלֹ֖שֶׁת הַגִּבֹּרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Far be it to me, Yahweh, from my doing this; [is it] the blood of the men who went with their lives? And not was he willing to drink them. These did [the] three of the mighty men.

en.L: And he said, "Far be it from me, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that I should do this! [Is it not] the blood of the men who went at [the risk of] their lives?" And he was not willing to drink it. These [things] the three mighty men did.
en.B: He said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, far be it from me to do this! Is it not the blood of men who went at the risk of their lives?" So he would not drink it. Such were the deeds of the three mighty warriors.
en.R: He said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, I could never do this! This water is like the blood of the men who risked their lives to get it." So he would not drink it. These are the brave things the three best warriors did.

es.L: Y dijo: «¡Lejos esté de mí, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, hacer esto! ¿[No es] la sangre de los hombres que fueron [arriesgando] sus vidas?». Y no quiso beberla. Estas [cosas] hicieron los tres valientes.
es.B: Dijo: «{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¡lejos de mí hacer esto! ¿No es la sangre de hombres que fueron arriesgando su vida?». Así que no quiso beberla. Tales fueron las hazañas de los tres guerreros valientes.
es.R: Dijo: «{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¡jamás podría hacer esto! Esta agua es como la sangre de los hombres que arriesgaron su vida para traerla». Así que no quiso beberla. Estas son las cosas valientes que hicieron los tres mejores guerreros.

fr.L: Et il dit : « Loin de moi, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, de faire cela ! [N’est-ce pas] le sang des hommes qui sont allés au [péril de] leur vie ? » Et il ne voulut pas la boire. Voilà ce que firent les trois vaillants hommes.
fr.B: Il dit : « {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, loin de moi de faire cela ! N’est-ce pas le sang des hommes qui sont allés là-bas au péril de leur vie ? » Il ne voulut donc pas la boire. Tels furent les exploits des trois vaillants guerriers.
fr.R: Il a dit : « {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je ne pourrai jamais faire cela ! Cette eau, c’est comme le sang des hommes qui ont risqué leur vie pour aller la chercher. » Il n’a donc pas voulu la boire. Voilà les actes courageux des trois meilleurs guerriers.

sw.L: Akasema, "Mbali nami, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nisifanye hivi! [Je, si] damu ya watu waliokwenda [kwa kuhatarisha] maisha yao?" Wala hakukubali kuyanywa. Mambo haya waliyafanya wale mashujaa watatu.
sw.B: Akasema, "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mbali nami kufanya hivi! Je, haya si damu ya watu waliokwenda kwa kuhatarisha maisha yao?" Kwa hiyo hakukubali kuyanywa. Hayo ndiyo matendo ya wale mashujaa watatu.
sw.R: Akasema, "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, siwezi kamwe kufanya hivi! Maji haya ni kama damu ya watu waliohatarisha maisha yao ili kuyaleta." Kwa hiyo hakuyanywa. Hayo ndiyo mambo ya ujasiri waliyoyafanya wale wapiganaji watatu hodari.

vi.L: Ông nói: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, không đời nào tôi làm điều này! [Chẳng phải đây là] máu của những người đã liều mạng sống mà đi sao?" Và ông không chịu uống. Đó [là những việc] ba dũng sĩ đã làm.
vi.B: Ông nói: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, không đời nào tôi làm điều đó! Chẳng phải đây là máu của những người đã liều mạng ra đi sao?" Vậy ông không chịu uống. Đó là những chiến công của ba dũng sĩ.
vi.R: Ông nói: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, tôi không bao giờ làm điều này được! Nước này như máu của những người đã liều mạng để lấy nó." Vậy ông không chịu uống. Đó là những việc can đảm ba chiến binh giỏi nhất đã làm.

decisions.choice: far be it from me: a strong refusal, made before Yahweh
decisions.reason: The phrase means "it would be a profane thing for me". By naming Yahweh, David makes the refusal almost an oath (compare 1 Samuel 24:7; 26:11).

decisions.choice: the blood of the men: the water cost the men their lives at risk, so it is like their blood
decisions.reason: Blood stands for life (Genesis 9:4; Leviticus 17:11), and blood was not to be drunk but poured out (Deuteronomy 12:16). Since the men risked their lives for the water, drinking it would be like drinking their blood. 1 Chronicles 11:19 adds "shall I drink", making the question complete.

decisions.choice: [Is it not] (Literal); Is it not (Balanced); This water is like (Readable); at the risk of
decisions.reason: The Hebrew question is cut short: "the blood of the men who went with their lives?" Each level supplies what completes it. "With their lives" means risking them, so all levels add "risk".

source.text: וַאֲבִישַׁ֞י אֲחִ֣י׀יוֹאָ֣ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֗ה ה֚וּא רֹ֣אשׁ הַשְּׁלֹשָׁ֔ה וְהוּא֙ עוֹרֵ֣ר אֶת־חֲנִית֔וֹ עַל־שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת חָלָ֑ל וְלוֹ־שֵׁ֖ם בַּשְּׁלֹשָֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Abishai brother of Joab son of Zeruiah, he [was] chief of the three; and he brandished his spear against three hundred slain, and to him [was] a name among the three.

en.L: And Abishai, [the] brother of Joab, son of Zeruiah, he [was] chief of the Three; and he wielded his spear against three hundred slain, and he had a name among the Three.
en.B: Abishai, the brother of Joab son of Zeruiah, was chief of the Three. He raised his spear against three hundred men and killed them, and he won a name alongside the Three.
en.R: Abishai, the brother of Joab son of Zeruiah, was the leader of the Three. He fought three hundred men with his spear and killed them. So he became as famous as the Three.

es.L: Y Abisai, hermano de Joab, hijo de Sarvia, él [era] jefe de los Tres; y blandió su lanza contra trescientos muertos, y tuvo nombre entre los Tres.
es.B: Abisai, el hermano de Joab hijo de Sarvia, era el jefe de los Tres. Levantó su lanza contra trescientos hombres y los mató, y se ganó un nombre junto a los Tres.
es.R: Abisai, el hermano de Joab hijo de Sarvia, era el líder de los Tres. Peleó con su lanza contra trescientos hombres y los mató. Así llegó a ser tan famoso como los Tres.

fr.L: Et Abishaï, le frère de Joab, fils de Tserouya, lui, [était] le chef des Trois ; et il brandit sa lance contre trois cents tués, et il eut un nom parmi les Trois.
fr.B: Abishaï, le frère de Joab, fils de Tserouya, était le chef des Trois. Il brandit sa lance contre trois cents hommes et les tua, et il se fit un nom à côté des Trois.
fr.R: Abishaï, le frère de Joab, fils de Tserouya, était le chef des Trois. Il a combattu trois cents hommes avec sa lance et il les a tués. Il est donc devenu aussi célèbre que les Trois.

sw.L: Abishai, ndugu wa Yoabu, mwana wa Seruya, yeye [alikuwa] mkuu wa wale Watatu; naye aliuinua mkuki wake dhidi ya watu mia tatu waliouawa, naye alikuwa na jina miongoni mwa wale Watatu.
sw.B: Abishai, ndugu wa Yoabu mwana wa Seruya, alikuwa mkuu wa wale Watatu. Aliuinua mkuki wake dhidi ya watu mia tatu akawaua, akapata jina pamoja na wale Watatu.
sw.R: Abishai, ndugu wa Yoabu mwana wa Seruya, alikuwa kiongozi wa wale Watatu. Alipigana na watu mia tatu kwa mkuki wake akawaua. Hivyo akawa maarufu kama wale Watatu.

vi.L: A-bi-sai, em Giô-áp, con trai Xê-ru-gia, là người đứng đầu nhóm Ba; ông vung giáo chống lại ba trăm người bị giết, và ông nổi danh trong nhóm Ba.
vi.B: A-bi-sai, em Giô-áp, con trai Xê-ru-gia, là người đứng đầu nhóm Ba. Ông vung giáo đánh ba trăm người và giết họ, và ông nổi danh ngang với nhóm Ba.
vi.R: A-bi-sai, em Giô-áp, con trai Xê-ru-gia, là người lãnh đạo nhóm Ba. Ông dùng giáo đánh ba trăm người và giết họ. Vì vậy ông nổi tiếng như nhóm Ba.

decisions.choice: chief of the Three: the spoken reading; some witnesses have "the Thirty"
decisions.reason: The written letters and the scribes' reading differ here as in verse 8, and the reading "the Three" is followed. But verse 19 says Abishai did not reach the Three, and verse 23 says the same of Benaiah with "the Thirty" in place of "the Three". So some witnesses, including the Syriac translation, read "chief of the Thirty" here and in verse 19, which gives a clearer sense: Abishai led the Thirty but did not rank with the Three. 1 Chronicles 11:20-21 has the same difficulty.

decisions.choice: Abishai son of Zeruiah: David's nephew and Joab's brother
decisions.reason: Zeruiah was David's sister (1 Chronicles 2:16), and her sons Joab, Abishai and Asahel were among David's leading men. Abishai was often at David's side (1 Samuel 26:6-9; 2 Samuel 16:9; 21:17).

decisions.choice: he had a name: he became famous
decisions.reason: "Name" here is reputation, as in 7:9 and 8:13.

decisions.choice: the Three (capital T)
decisions.reason: Where "the three" or "the thirty" stands alone as the name of the group of warriors, all levels write it with a capital letter, the Three and the Thirty, so the reader can tell the group from the number. "The three mighty men" keeps a small letter.

decisions.choice: "les Trois", "les Trente" with capitals
decisions.reason: Names of the two groups of warriors, capitalised as the English capitalises them.

source.text: מִן־הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה֙ הֲכִ֣י נִכְבָּ֔ד וַיְהִ֥י לָהֶ֖ם לְשָׂ֑ר וְעַד־הַשְּׁלֹשָׁ֖ה לֹא־בָֽא׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Than the three was he not honored? And he became to them for commander; and to the three not he came.

en.L: Above the Three was he not honored? And he became their commander, but to the Three he did not come.
en.B: Was he not honored above the Three? He became their commander, but he did not reach the rank of the Three.
en.R: He was honored more than the Three and became their commander. But he was never one of the Three.

es.L: ¿No fue él más honrado que los Tres? Y llegó a ser su jefe, pero a los Tres no llegó.
es.B: ¿No fue honrado más que los Tres? Llegó a ser su jefe, pero no alcanzó el rango de los Tres.
es.R: Fue más honrado que los Tres y llegó a ser su jefe. Pero nunca fue uno de los Tres.

fr.L: Plus que les Trois n’était-il pas honoré ? Et il devint leur chef ; mais jusqu’aux Trois il n’arriva pas.
fr.B: N’était-il pas plus honoré que les Trois ? Il devint leur chef, mais il n’atteignit pas le rang des Trois.
fr.R: Il était plus honoré que les Trois et il est devenu leur chef. Mais il n’a jamais fait partie des Trois.

sw.L: Je, hakuheshimiwa kuliko wale Watatu? Akawa jemadari wao, lakini hakufikia wale Watatu.
sw.B: Je, hakuheshimiwa kuliko wale Watatu? Akawa kamanda wao, lakini hakufikia cheo cha wale Watatu.
sw.R: Aliheshimiwa kuliko wale Watatu, akawa kamanda wao. Lakini hakuwa kamwe mmoja wa wale Watatu.

vi.L: Chẳng phải ông được tôn trọng hơn nhóm Ba sao? Ông trở thành chỉ huy của họ, nhưng ông không đạt tới nhóm Ba.
vi.B: Chẳng phải ông được tôn trọng hơn nhóm Ba sao? Ông trở thành chỉ huy của họ, nhưng không được kể vào hàng nhóm Ba.
vi.R: Ông được tôn trọng hơn nhóm Ba và trở thành chỉ huy của họ. Nhưng ông không bao giờ thuộc về nhóm Ba.

decisions.choice: was he not honored above the Three? a question that expects the answer yes
alternatives: of the Three he was the most honored
he was the most honored of the Thirty
decisions.reason: The small question word followed by "that" asks "is it not so that ...?", which means he was indeed honored. If the group in verse 18 was the Thirty (see the note there), the sense is "he was the most honored of the Thirty". 1 Chronicles 11:21 has a slightly different wording, "of the Three, in the second rank, he was honored".

decisions.choice: to the Three he did not come: he did not reach their rank
decisions.reason: "Come to" means to attain to or be counted with. Abishai led others but was not one of the top three heroes. The same is said of Benaiah in verse 23.

decisions.choice: He was honored more than the Three (statement)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the question that expects "yes" as a plain statement.

source.text: וּבְנָיָ֨הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹיָדָ֧ע בֶּן־אִֽישׁ־חַ֛יִל רַב־פְּעָלִ֖ים מִֽקַּבְצְאֵ֑ל ה֣וּא הִכָּ֗ה אֵ֣ת שְׁנֵ֤י אֲרִאֵל֙ מוֹאָ֔ב וְ֠הוּא יָרַ֞ד וְהִכָּ֧ה אֶֽת־הָאֲרִ֛י בְּת֥וֹךְ הַבֹּ֖אר בְּי֥וֹם הַשָּֽׁלֶג׃

records.literal_gloss: And Benaiah son of Jehoiada son of a man of valor great of deeds from Kabzeel; he struck down [the] two ariel of Moab; and he went down and struck down the lion in [the] middle of the pit on [the] day of the snow.

en.L: And Benaiah son of Jehoiada [was the] son of a man of valor, great of deeds, from Kabzeel. He struck down the two champions of Moab; and he went down and struck down the lion in [the] middle of the pit on the day of the snow.
en.B: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was the son of a brave man from Kabzeel who did great deeds. He struck down the two champions of Moab. He also went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.
en.R: Benaiah son of Jehoiada came from Kabzeel. He was the son of a brave man who had done great things. Benaiah killed the two greatest fighters of Moab. And one day when there was snow on the ground, he went down into a pit and killed a lion there.

es.L: Y Benaía hijo de Joiada [era] hijo de un hombre valiente, grande en hazañas, de Cabseel. Él mató a los dos campeones de Moab; y descendió y mató al león en medio del foso el día de la nieve.
es.B: Benaía hijo de Joiada era hijo de un hombre valiente de Cabseel que hizo grandes hazañas. Mató a los dos campeones de Moab. También bajó a un foso un día de nieve y mató a un león.
es.R: Benaía hijo de Joiada era de Cabseel. Era hijo de un hombre valiente que había hecho grandes cosas. Benaía mató a los dos mejores guerreros de Moab. Y un día en que había nieve en el suelo, bajó a un foso y mató allí a un león.

fr.L: Et Benaya, fils de Yehoyada, [était] fils d’un homme vaillant, aux grands exploits, de Qabtséel. Il frappa les deux champions de Moab ; et il descendit et frappa le lion au milieu de la fosse, un jour de neige.
fr.B: Benaya, fils de Yehoyada, était le fils d’un homme vaillant de Qabtséel, qui avait accompli de grands exploits. Il abattit les deux champions de Moab. Il descendit aussi dans une fosse, un jour de neige, et y tua un lion.
fr.R: Benaya, fils de Yehoyada, venait de Qabtséel. C’était le fils d’un homme courageux qui avait fait de grandes choses. Benaya a tué les deux meilleurs combattants de Moab. Et un jour où il y avait de la neige par terre, il est descendu dans une fosse et il y a tué un lion.

sw.L: Na Benaya mwana wa Yehoyada [alikuwa] mwana wa mtu shujaa, mwenye matendo makuu, wa Kabseeli. Aliwapiga mashujaa wawili wa Moabu; naye akashuka akampiga simba katikati ya shimo siku ya theluji.
sw.B: Benaya mwana wa Yehoyada alikuwa mwana wa mtu shujaa wa Kabseeli aliyefanya matendo makuu. Aliwaua mashujaa wawili wa Moabu. Pia alishuka ndani ya shimo siku ya theluji akamwua simba.
sw.R: Benaya mwana wa Yehoyada alitoka Kabseeli. Alikuwa mwana wa mtu shujaa aliyefanya mambo makuu. Benaya aliwaua wapiganaji wawili hodari kuliko wote wa Moabu. Tena siku moja theluji ilipokuwa imefunika ardhi, alishuka ndani ya shimo akamwua simba humo.

vi.L: Bê-na-gia con trai Giê-hô-gia-đa [là] con một dũng sĩ, có nhiều chiến công, ở Cáp-xê-ên. Ông đánh giết hai dũng tướng của Mô-áp; ông cũng đi xuống giết con sư tử giữa hố vào ngày có tuyết.
vi.B: Bê-na-gia con trai Giê-hô-gia-đa là con của một dũng sĩ ở Cáp-xê-ên, người đã lập nhiều chiến công. Ông đánh giết hai dũng tướng của Mô-áp. Vào một ngày tuyết rơi, ông cũng xuống một cái hố và giết một con sư tử.
vi.R: Bê-na-gia con trai Giê-hô-gia-đa quê ở Cáp-xê-ên. Ông là con của một người can đảm đã làm nhiều việc lớn. Bê-na-gia đã giết hai chiến binh giỏi nhất của Mô-áp. Có một ngày tuyết phủ mặt đất, ông xuống một cái hố và giết một con sư tử ở đó.

decisions.choice: son of a man of valor, great of deeds: the spoken reading
decisions.reason: The written letters read "son of a living man", which the scribes' reading corrects to "son of a man of valor". "Great of deeds" may describe the father or Benaiah himself; the Hebrew joins it to the father. 1 Chronicles 11:22 has the same words.

decisions.choice: the two champions of Moab: the sense of "ariel" is uncertain
alternatives: the two sons of Ariel of Moab
decisions.reason: The word may mean "lion of God", a title for a great warrior, and that is how it is taken here. The Greek translation reads "the two sons of Ariel of Moab", as if Ariel were a person. The same word is used of an altar hearth (Ezekiel 43:15-16) and as a name for Jerusalem (Isaiah 29:1-2), but neither fits here.

decisions.choice: killed the lion in a pit on a snowy day: a famous feat
decisions.reason: The article ("the lion", "the day of the snow") suggests a well-known story. A lion trapped in a pit or cistern would be most dangerous, and snow made the footing slippery. Lions lived in Israel's hills and thickets (1 Samuel 17:34-36; Judges 14:5).

decisions.choice: Benaiah son of Jehoiada: commander of David's guard and later of Solomon's army
decisions.reason: Benaiah was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites (8:18; 20:23). He later supported Solomon and became commander of the army (1 Kings 1:38; 2:35).

decisions.choice: champions (Balanced); greatest fighters (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "champions" and Readable "greatest fighters", following the sense chosen in the meaning note.

source.text: וְהוּא־הִכָּה֩ אֶת־אִ֨ישׁ מִצְרִ֜י אִ֣ישׁ מַרְאֶ֗ה וּבְיַ֤ד הַמִּצְרִי֙ חֲנִ֔ית וַיֵּ֥רֶד אֵלָ֖יו בַּשָּׁ֑בֶט וַיִּגְזֹ֤ל אֶֽת־הַחֲנִית֙ מִיַּ֣ד הַמִּצְרִ֔י וַיַּהַרְגֵ֖הוּ בַּחֲנִיתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he struck down an Egyptian man, a man of appearance; and in [the] hand of the Egyptian [was] a spear, and he went down to him with the staff and seized the spear from [the] hand of the Egyptian and killed him with his [own] spear.

en.L: And he struck down an Egyptian man, a man of [impressive] appearance; and in the hand of the Egyptian [was] a spear, but he went down to him with a staff and snatched the spear from the hand of the Egyptian and killed him with his own spear.
en.B: He also struck down an Egyptian, an impressive-looking man. The Egyptian had a spear in his hand, but Benaiah went down against him with a club, snatched the spear from the Egyptian's grip and killed him with his own weapon.
en.R: He also killed an Egyptian, a huge man. The Egyptian held a spear, but Benaiah went to fight him with only a club. Benaiah grabbed the spear from the Egyptian's hand and killed him with it.

es.L: Y mató a un hombre egipcio, un hombre de [gran] apariencia; y en la mano del egipcio [había] una lanza, pero él bajó contra él con un palo, y arrebató la lanza de la mano del egipcio y lo mató con su propia lanza.
es.B: También mató a un egipcio, un hombre de aspecto imponente. El egipcio tenía una lanza en la mano, pero Benaía bajó contra él con un garrote, le arrebató la lanza de la mano y lo mató con su propia arma.
es.R: También mató a un egipcio, un hombre enorme. El egipcio tenía una lanza, pero Benaía fue a pelear con él solo con un garrote. Benaía le arrancó la lanza de la mano al egipcio y lo mató con ella.

fr.L: Et il frappa un homme égyptien, un homme d’[impressionnante] apparence ; et dans la main de l’Égyptien [il y avait] une lance, mais il descendit vers lui avec un bâton, arracha la lance de la main de l’Égyptien et le tua avec sa propre lance.
fr.B: Il abattit aussi un Égyptien, un homme d’une stature impressionnante. L’Égyptien avait une lance à la main, mais Benaya descendit contre lui avec un gourdin, arracha la lance de la main de l’Égyptien et le tua avec sa propre arme.
fr.R: Il a aussi tué un Égyptien, un homme énorme. L’Égyptien tenait une lance, mais Benaya est allé le combattre avec seulement un gourdin. Benaya a arraché la lance de la main de l’Égyptien et l’a tué avec.

sw.L: Akampiga mtu Mmisri, mtu wa sura [ya kutisha]; na mkononi mwa Mmisri [kulikuwa na] mkuki, lakini akamshukia na fimbo, akaunyakua mkuki kutoka mkononi mwa Mmisri, akamwua kwa mkuki wake mwenyewe.
sw.B: Pia alimwua Mmisri mmoja, mtu wa umbo la kutisha. Mmisri huyo alikuwa na mkuki mkononi, lakini Benaya akamwendea na rungu, akaunyakua mkuki kutoka mkononi mwa Mmisri, akamwua kwa silaha yake mwenyewe.
sw.R: Pia alimwua Mmisri mmoja, mtu mkubwa sana. Mmisri huyo alishika mkuki, lakini Benaya akaenda kupigana naye akiwa na rungu tu. Benaya akaunyakua mkuki kutoka mkononi mwa Mmisri, akamwua kwa mkuki huo.

vi.L: Ông đánh giết một người Ai Cập, một người có dáng vẻ [đáng sợ]; trong tay người Ai Cập [có] một cây giáo, nhưng ông cầm gậy đi xuống đánh hắn, giật cây giáo khỏi tay người Ai Cập và dùng chính cây giáo của hắn mà giết hắn.
vi.B: Ông cũng đánh giết một người Ai Cập có dáng vẻ oai vệ. Người Ai Cập cầm cây giáo trong tay, nhưng Bê-na-gia chỉ cầm gậy đi xuống đánh hắn, giật cây giáo khỏi tay hắn và dùng chính vũ khí của hắn mà giết hắn.
vi.R: Ông cũng giết một người Ai Cập to lớn. Người Ai Cập cầm một cây giáo, nhưng Bê-na-gia chỉ cầm một cây gậy đi ra đánh hắn. Bê-na-gia giật cây giáo khỏi tay người Ai Cập và dùng nó giết hắn.

decisions.choice: a man of impressive appearance: the spoken reading
alternatives: a man of great height (1 Chronicles 11:23)
decisions.reason: The written letters have "who [was] of appearance", which the scribes' reading corrects to "a man of appearance". The phrase means a man notable for his looks, here his size: 1 Chronicles 11:23 says he was five cubits tall and that his spear was like a weaver's beam, as was said of Goliath (1 Samuel 17:7).

decisions.choice: with a staff ... with his own spear: the champion is killed by his own weapon
decisions.reason: Benaiah came against an armed man with only a club, took his spear and killed him with it, as David killed Goliath with Goliath's own sword (1 Samuel 17:51).

decisions.choice: an impressive-looking man (Balanced); a huge man (Readable); club
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the Egyptian was big, which is what "a man of appearance" means here. The word for the staff is the ordinary word for a rod or club.

source.text: אֵ֣לֶּה עָשָׂ֔ה בְּנָיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־יְהוֹיָדָ֑ע וְלוֹ־שֵׁ֖ם בִּשְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה הַגִּבֹּרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: These did Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and to him [was] a name among [the] three the mighty men.

en.L: These [things] Benaiah son of Jehoiada did, and he had a name among the three mighty men.
en.B: Such were the deeds of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he won a name alongside the three mighty warriors.
en.R: These are the brave things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did. He became as famous as the three best warriors.

es.L: Estas [cosas] hizo Benaía hijo de Joiada, y tuvo nombre entre los tres valientes.
es.B: Tales fueron las hazañas de Benaía hijo de Joiada, y se ganó un nombre junto a los tres guerreros valientes.
es.R: Estas son las cosas valientes que hizo Benaía hijo de Joiada. Llegó a ser tan famoso como los tres mejores guerreros.

fr.L: Voilà ce que fit Benaya, fils de Yehoyada, et il eut un nom parmi les trois vaillants hommes.
fr.B: Tels furent les exploits de Benaya, fils de Yehoyada, et il se fit un nom à côté des trois vaillants guerriers.
fr.R: Voilà les actes courageux de Benaya, fils de Yehoyada. Il est devenu aussi célèbre que les trois meilleurs guerriers.

sw.L: Mambo haya aliyafanya Benaya mwana wa Yehoyada, naye alikuwa na jina miongoni mwa wale mashujaa watatu.
sw.B: Hayo ndiyo matendo ya Benaya mwana wa Yehoyada, naye akapata jina pamoja na wale mashujaa watatu.
sw.R: Hayo ndiyo mambo ya ujasiri aliyoyafanya Benaya mwana wa Yehoyada. Akawa maarufu kama wale wapiganaji watatu hodari kuliko wote.

vi.L: Đó [là những việc] Bê-na-gia con trai Giê-hô-gia-đa đã làm, và ông nổi danh trong ba dũng sĩ.
vi.B: Đó là những chiến công của Bê-na-gia con trai Giê-hô-gia-đa, và ông nổi danh ngang với ba dũng sĩ.
vi.R: Đó là những việc can đảm Bê-na-gia con trai Giê-hô-gia-đa đã làm. Ông nổi tiếng như ba chiến binh giỏi nhất.

decisions.choice: a name among the three mighty men: fame equal to theirs, though not one of them
decisions.reason: "Among" here means "alongside" or "as well as", since verse 23 says he did not reach the Three. The wording matches what is said of Abishai in verse 18.

source.text: מִן־הַשְּׁלֹשִׁ֣ים נִכְבָּ֔ד וְאֶל־הַשְּׁלֹשָׁ֖ה לֹא־בָ֑א וַיְשִׂמֵ֥הוּ דָוִ֖ד אֶל־מִשְׁמַעְתּֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Than the thirty honored, and to the three not he came; and set him David over his bodyguard.

en.L: Above the Thirty he was honored, but to the Three he did not come; and David set him over his bodyguard.
en.B: He was honored above the Thirty, but he did not reach the rank of the Three. And David put him in charge of his bodyguard.
en.R: He was honored more than the Thirty, but he was never one of the Three. David made him the leader of his own guards.

es.L: Fue más honrado que los Treinta, pero a los Tres no llegó; y David lo puso sobre su guardia personal.
es.B: Fue honrado más que los Treinta, pero no alcanzó el rango de los Tres. Y David lo puso al mando de su guardia personal.
es.R: Fue más honrado que los Treinta, pero nunca fue uno de los Tres. David lo nombró jefe de su propia guardia.

fr.L: Plus que les Trente il fut honoré, mais jusqu’aux Trois il n’arriva pas ; et David le mit à la tête de sa garde personnelle.
fr.B: Il fut plus honoré que les Trente, mais il n’atteignit pas le rang des Trois. Et David lui confia le commandement de sa garde personnelle.
fr.R: Il était plus honoré que les Trente, mais il n’a jamais fait partie des Trois. David a fait de lui le chef de ses propres gardes.

sw.L: Aliheshimiwa kuliko wale Thelathini, lakini hakufikia wale Watatu; naye Daudi akamweka juu ya walinzi wake.
sw.B: Aliheshimiwa kuliko wale Thelathini, lakini hakufikia cheo cha wale Watatu. Naye Daudi akamweka kuwa mkuu wa walinzi wake.
sw.R: Aliheshimiwa kuliko wale Thelathini, lakini hakuwa kamwe mmoja wa wale Watatu. Daudi akamfanya kuwa kiongozi wa walinzi wake mwenyewe.

vi.L: Ông được tôn trọng hơn nhóm Ba Mươi, nhưng không đạt tới nhóm Ba; và Đa-vít lập ông chỉ huy đội cận vệ của mình.
vi.B: Ông được tôn trọng hơn nhóm Ba Mươi, nhưng không được kể vào hàng nhóm Ba. Đa-vít lập ông chỉ huy đội cận vệ của mình.
vi.R: Ông được tôn trọng hơn nhóm Ba Mươi, nhưng không bao giờ thuộc về nhóm Ba. Đa-vít cho ông làm người chỉ huy đội cận vệ của vua.

decisions.choice: over his bodyguard: in command of the men who guarded the king
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to hear" and means those who listen and obey, here the king's personal guard (1 Samuel 22:14). This fits Benaiah's command of the Cherethites and the Pelethites (8:18; 20:23).

decisions.choice: honored above the Thirty, not reaching the Three: as Abishai in verse 19
decisions.reason: Benaiah, like Abishai, stood between the two groups. 1 Chronicles 11:25 says the same.

source.text: עֲשָׂה־אֵ֥ל אֲחִֽי־יוֹאָ֖ב בַּשְּׁלֹשִׁ֑ים אֶלְחָנָ֥ן בֶּן־דֹּד֖וֹ בֵּ֥ית לָֽחֶם׃

records.literal_gloss: Asahel brother of Joab among the thirty; Elhanan son of Dodo [of] Bethlehem,

en.L: Asahel, [the] brother of Joab, [was] among the Thirty; Elhanan son of Dodo [of] Bethlehem,
en.B: Among the Thirty were Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem,
en.R: These were also among the Thirty: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem,

es.L: Asael, hermano de Joab, [estaba] entre los Treinta; Elhanán hijo de Dodo, [de] Belén,

decisions.choice: Uriah the Hittite: Bathsheba's husband
decisions.reason: The list ends with Uriah, whom David had killed after taking his wife (11:3-17). Placing his name last, among David's most faithful warriors, recalls that story. 1 Chronicles 11:41-47 goes on with sixteen more names.

decisions.choice: thirty-seven in all: how the total is counted is not stated
decisions.reason: Verses 24-39 name thirty-one men. With the Three (verses 8-12), Abishai and Benaiah, that makes thirty-six; if Joab, the commander of the army, is counted too, the total is thirty-seven. Other ways of counting are possible, and "the Thirty" seems to be the name of the group rather than its exact size.
